why_combined: User requested larger passes. The remaining material is coherent enough to close in one archive if split internally into R03A/R03B/R04 sections.
reading_quality: Good for control flow, method/event names, and mental model. Dense code screenshots are summarized semantically rather than copied line-for-line where tiny text is not fully readable.
key_ideas: JwtBearerHandler authentication starts by giving OnMessageReceived a chance to supply a token, then usually reads Authorization: Bearer from the header.
Token validation creates ClaimsPrincipal on success and AuthenticationFailed on failure.
JWT events let app code hook MessageReceived, TokenValidated, AuthenticationFailed, Challenge, and Forbidden behavior.
Challenge means no valid authenticated result and asks the client to authenticate; Forbid means authenticated/known user cannot access.
OIDC sign-in bridge uses challenge to external provider, authorization code + PKCE, callback, token exchange, and cookie sign-in to establish local session.
